The relative use of ἵνα is found occasionally in Attic writers. In Bonitz’ Index the only instances given are ἵνα περ, Problems 876a 33, and ἵνα in a quotation from Euripides, Rhetoric 1371b 32 and Prob. 917a 14; but as examples occur sporadically from the time of Homer to that of Lucian, the construction must at any rate have been possible to the author of the de Spiritu.

The liver cannot be kept warm otherwise, because it has no air-duct to admit the breath to it: so when the venous blood is cooled, the liver grows cold.
